LHX.sentence: L3Harris slipped a touch and sits well off its high, but it's the smallest of the big defense contractors and tends to trade a little cheaper than the others — defense budgets are steady, so nothing has really changed about the business.

ASML.sentence: ASML has pulled back more than a fifth from its peak, which is unusual for a company that's the only one in the world making a certain kind of chipmaking machine — the business hasn't changed, the stock just got cheaper.

LIN.sentence: Linde is quiet — they supply oxygen, nitrogen and other gases under long contracts and nudge prices up a little each year, and that steady grind is the whole story.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is calm — its Azure cloud business keeps growing fast as companies rent computing power for AI, and the story keeps grinding along without drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher is barely moved; the lab-equipment and bioprocessing slump they supply into is scraping along the bottom, and it's not yet clear it's turning back up.

CVX.sentence: Chevron is steady, and its profits look big right now mainly because fighting involving Iran has pushed oil prices well above normal — that's the oil price doing the work, not the company, so the stock will drift back when tensions ease.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow dropped sharply and is now down nearly half from its high, an unusually steep fall for a company still growing fast — big companies and government agencies keep signing multi-year deals for its workflow and AI tools, so the business looks intact even as the stock got hammered.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore slipped even as copper prices have been surging, which leaves this miner-and-trader lagging behind a metal it digs out of the ground — a gap that sometimes closes later.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta dipped slightly; the price it gets per ton of crushed stone is still creeping up, which is the part that actually matters, even though a shift in what it sold made the headline price number look softer than it really is.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA barely moved, though a weakening Mexican peso is a mild headwind since most of this Latin American Coke bottler's sales come in pesos.

UBER.sentence: Uber drifted down a bit, but people keep booking more rides and food orders through the app than ever and there's no sign robotaxis are pulling business away yet — so for now it's a question about the future, not a problem today.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant that moves goods around the world on ships, is trading well below what its fleet would cost to replace — a classic sign the stock is cheap at the low point of the shipping cycle.

MA.sentence: Mastercard slipped with the broader market, but people keep tapping their cards more than ever, and it's trading unusually close to rival Visa rather than at its normal premium.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical-robot company pulled back and is now at its cheapest in years relative to its own history, even as hospitals keep doing more operations with its machines — and every operation sells more instruments and supplies.

NVDA.sentence: Nvidia fell along with the rest of the AI names because two of its biggest customers, Google's parent and Amazon, are now spending more on computing gear than their businesses bring in and borrowing the rest — nothing changed at Nvidia itself, but whether those customers can keep paying is the whole question.
